name: The Weight of Blue
description: Experimental director Tomás Ejiogu-Lindqvist spent six years developing this 90-minute neural-feed experience in which the viewer does not inhabit a character — they inhabit a color. The film simulates consciousness as pure chromatic sensation, translating grief, memory, and longing into shifting blue-spectrum wavelengths that interact with the viewer's proprioception and emotional recall centers. There is no narrative. There is no dialogue. The BCI requirements are steep enough that Tier 1 access is essentially impossible.
cultural_impact: The Weight of Blue redefined what neural-feed art could demand of its audience, establishing the 'pure sensation' subgenre and making Ejiogu-Lindqvist the most discussed experimental filmmaker in M88 history.
story_hooks: A Tier 5 collector is paying extraordinary sums for the original uncompressed neural-feed master — the party learns the buyer intends to weaponize its emotional manipulation properties.
One of the twelve affected viewers has developed a synesthetic condition that lets them perceive encrypted data transmissions as color — and someone wants to exploit that ability.
Ejiogu-Lindqvist has disappeared mid-production on a follow-up, leaving behind only a partial neural-feed that causes disorientation in anyone who accesses it.
